candidate_e10_results.termination_reason: Post-severance cutback exhaustion at u = 0.00998 mm (>99.7% load loss achieved)

scientific_conclusions: Candidate E10 (9,164 physical elements, 27,694 DOFs) achieves complete dual-crack fracture kinematics matching the published benchmark: notch crack initiates, deflects smoothly into the off-axis circular hole, arrests at the hole perimeter, reloads elastically, nucleates a secondary flank crack, and snaps through to complete right-ligament severance.

Computational cost is dramatically reduced: -57.51% physical elements, -57.23% active DOFs, -63.47% solver CPU time (1,180 s vs 3,230 s), and -60.06% walltime (32 min vs 80 min), representing a 2.74x computational speedup.
Peak force parity is verified: primary peak load is 0.5597 kN at u = 0.00536 mm, within +0.36% of the F1685 21,569-element adapted baseline (0.5577 kN at u = 0.00534 mm).
Energy consistency is verified: stored elastic strain energy relaxes by 99.65% (from 1.906 mJ down to 6.59 uJ), while dissipated fracture energy plateaus at 2.727 mJ (within -8.92% of F1685).

Post-severance termination: at u = 0.00998 mm (Step 2 Inc 292), with >99.7% load loss and the specimen completely cut in two, post-fracture rigid-body separation naturally encountered cutback exhaustion (Exit 1), with 100% of the physical fracture process fully resolved.
